Information received since September points to a still-strong labor market and solid household spending, but weak business fixed investment and exports with inflation running below 2%. In line with New Keynesian evidence that inflation dynamics hinge on expected inflation and real activity (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido) and VAR findings that monetary expansions have short-run real effects (Sims), the 25 bp rate cut and “ample reserves” operations (T-bill purchases and repos) should support activity via the liquidity effect. Given the central role of investment in driving business-cycle amplitude and declines in real GDP, the Committee’s insurance easing is consistent with rules-based stabilization insights (McCallum and Nelson, 1999; B. Friedman) while appropriately flagging risks from low market-based inflation compensation and global uncertainty. Overall tone: mildly positive but cautious.
